name: univest upcoming results :: screener MCP + Sep 2026 filter

nodes.name: Every 5 minutes
nodes.notes: Testing cadence. The MCP build/start steps are idempotent, so a tick that lands on a healthy server costs one tools/list probe.

nodes.name: Build MCP Server

parameters.command:
set -e
DIR=/home/node/.n8n/screener-mcp-server
REPO=https://github.com/shivamg194-lab/screener-mcp-server.git
TARBALL=https://codeload.github.com/shivamg194-lab/screener-mcp-server/tar.gz/refs/heads/main

# --- fetch or update the repo (git if present, tarball fallback) ---
if [ -d "$DIR/.git" ]; then
  git -C "$DIR" pull --ff-only || true
elif command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  git clone --depth 1 "$REPO" "$DIR"
else
  echo 'git not found in container, falling back to tarball'
  mkdir -p "$DIR"
  wget -qO- "$TARBALL" | tar xz --strip-components=1 -C "$DIR"
fi

cd "$DIR"

# --- install deps INCLUDING devDependencies ---
# The n8n image sets NODE_ENV=production, which makes npm skip devDeps and
# leaves typescript missing, so the build would fail. Force it here.
if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then
  NODE_ENV=development npm ci --include=dev --no-audit --no-fund \
    || NODE_ENV=development npm install --include=dev --no-audit --no-fund
else
  NODE_ENV=development npm install --include=dev --no-audit --no-fund
fi

# --- build (call tsc directly; `npm run build` also runs chmod) ---
./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json

test -f dist/index.js || { echo 'BUILD_FAILED: dist/index.js missing'; exit 1; }
echo "BUILD_OK node=$(node -v) dir=$DIR"

nodes.notes: Unchanged from the supervisor workflow: check out screener-mcp-server, install devDeps, tsc. Prints BUILD_OK.

nodes.name: Start If Not Running

parameters.command:
DIR=/home/node/.n8n/screener-mcp-server
PORT=3123
LOG=/home/node/.n8n/screener-mcp.log
PROBE='{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'

# --- already listening? then do nothing (idempotent restart-safe) ---
if wget -q -O /dev/null --timeout=3 \
     --header='Content-Type: application/json' \
     --header='Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
     --post-data="$PROBE" "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/mcp" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "ALREADY_RUNNING port=$PORT"
  exit 0
fi

cd "$DIR"
# Detach so the process outlives this node's execution. It still dies if the
# n8n container restarts - that is what the 10-minute schedule is for.
if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  TRANSPORT=http PORT=$PORT setsid node dist/index.js >> "$LOG" 2>&1 &
else
  ( TRANSPORT=http PORT=$PORT nohup node dist/index.js >> "$LOG" 2>&1 & )
fi

sleep 3
echo "STARTED port=$PORT log=$LOG"
tail -n 5 "$LOG" 2>/dev/null || true

nodes.notes: Unchanged from the supervisor workflow: idempotent - probes the port first and only starts a detached server if nothing answers.

nodes.name: Wait 5s
nodes.notes: Give a freshly started server time to bind the port before the health check.

nodes.name: Health Check (tools/list)
nodes.notes: Unchanged from the supervisor workflow. neverError is on so an unhealthy server routes to the failure branch instead of aborting the run.

nodes.name: Healthy?
nodes.notes: true only when tools/list came back with at least one tool. Everything downstream can assume a live MCP endpoint.

nodes.name: Fetch Upcoming Results
nodes.notes: The stock list. Answers { data: { "<result date>": [ {finCode, compName, nseSymbol, bseSymbol, ...} ] } }. fullResponse keeps the status code so a bad answer can be logged with its payload instead of aborting the run. MOVE THE BEARER TOKEN INTO AN N8N CREDENTIAL BEFORE THIS LEAVES TESTING.

nodes.name: Flatten Upcoming Results
nodes.notes: Date buckets -> one item per stock, with the NSE series suffix stripped (DHTL-SM -> DHTL, KOTYARK-BE -> KOTYARK) because screener.in only knows the bare ticker. Anything that will not reduce to a safe ticker is marked usable:false and never reaches the shell.

nodes.name: Query Screener MCP
nodes.notes: Runs once per stock. node -e posts one tools/call for screener_get_financial_statement (quarters) and prints one JSON document. Falls back from consolidated to standalone when consolidated is missing or empty. Never exits non-zero.

nodes.name: Filter On Sep 2026 Column
nodes.notes: Parses every answer to JSON (structuredContent first, Markdown table parser as fallback), then keeps only stocks whose periods contain the target column. Change TARGET_PERIOD at the top when the quarter rolls over. Returns a single item so the log writer fires once.

nodes.name: Write Run Log

parameters.command:
=# One append per run, for both outcomes:
#
#   qualified.jsonl  which stock qualified and when (ts + resultDate + the
#                    matched column, plus every period screener showed)
#   failures.jsonl   when it failed, why, and the payload it failed for
#                    (the API record, and whatever the MCP server said)
#   runs.jsonl       one summary line per run
#
# Heredocs are quoted, so a $ or a backtick inside the JSON stays literal.
set -u
DIR=/home/node/.n8n/univest-results/logs
mkdir -p "$DIR"

append() {
  BODY=$(cat)
  if [ -n "$BODY" ]; then printf "%s\n" "$BODY" >> "$DIR/$1"; fi
  return 0
}

append qualified.jsonl <<'Q_EOF'
{{ $json.logs.qualifiedJsonl }}
Q_EOF

append failures.jsonl <<'F_EOF'
{{ $json.logs.failuresJsonl }}
F_EOF

append runs.jsonl <<'R_EOF'
{{ $json.logs.runJsonl }}
R_EOF

echo "LOGGED run={{ $json.runId }} target={{ $json.targetPeriod }} checked={{ $json.checked }} qualified={{ $json.qualified }} notQualified={{ $json.notQualified }} failed={{ $json.failed }} skipped={{ $json.skipped }}"
wc -l "$DIR"/*.jsonl 2>/dev/null || true

nodes.notes: Appends qualified.jsonl, failures.jsonl and runs.jsonl under /home/node/.n8n/univest-results/logs. One shell run per workflow execution, not per stock.

nodes.name: Return Qualified Data
nodes.notes: One item per qualifying stock, carrying the parsed quarterly table. When nothing qualified it emits a single run summary - a normal outcome, not an error.

nodes.name: Dump MCP Log
nodes.notes: The server did not answer tools/list. Its own log is the only thing that says why.

nodes.name: Build Health Failure
nodes.notes: Builds the failures.jsonl record for a dead MCP server, with the tail of its log as the payload. Built in code, not in an expression, so the log writer downstream only has to interpolate one ready-made string.

nodes.name: Write Health Failure

parameters.command:
# Same two files as the healthy branch, so the logs are a complete
# record of every run and not just of the ones that got as far as a stock.
set -u
DIR=/home/node/.n8n/univest-results/logs
mkdir -p "$DIR"

cat >> "$DIR/failures.jsonl" <<'E_EOF'
{{ $json.logLine }}
E_EOF

cat >> "$DIR/runs.jsonl" <<'R_EOF'
{{ $json.runLine }}
R_EOF

echo "LOGGED mcp-health failure run={{ $json.runId }} to $DIR/failures.jsonl"

nodes.notes: Appends the health failure to failures.jsonl and a zero-checked summary to runs.jsonl.

nodes.name: MCP Unhealthy
nodes.notes: Terminal state for the unhealthy branch: a parseable failure document rather than a silently empty run.
